coverage.scope: Every public, non-fork repository the user owns except the profile repository and activity_exclusions; default branches; authored non-merge commits; all time

methodology: Candles cover UTC days, Monday-start weeks, months, quarters or years. The index starts at zero before the first collected commit. Commits are ordered by Git committer timestamp, then SHA. For each commit, additions raise the index before deletions lower it. Open is the previous close; high and low capture those constructed excursions; close is cumulative additions minus deletions. The additions-first convention is a visualization rule, not a measured within-commit timeline. Only commits authored by the configured GitHub user and reachable from the default branches of their public, non-fork repositories are counted. Merge commits are excluded to avoid recounting merged changes. Identical SHAs across repositories are counted once. Binary-file changes may have zero line statistics. Line volume is activity, not productivity or financial value.
